kjv: whom she brought up for Adriel
note: yaldah means 'she bore'. The KJV softened it to 'brought up' because Michal was childless (6:23) and Adriel married her sister Merab (1 Sam 18:19); some Hebrew MSS and LXX read 'Merab' here. MT says Michal.
chadashah ('new', feminine) has no noun; what was new (sword, armor, belt) is not stated.

kjv: slew [the brother of] Goliath the Gittite
note: MT says Elhanan killed Goliath the Gittite; the KJV inserts 'the brother of' (italics) from the parallel 1 Chr 20:5 ('Lahmi the brother of Goliath') to harmonize with 1 Sam 17. Context: Goliath (as the Hebrew says) (high confidence). MT and LXX both read 'Goliath'. The text is visibly disturbed ('oregim, 'weavers', seems copied from the line's end), and 1 Chr 20:5 may preserve an original 'Lahmi the brother of Goliath'; but no witness to Samuel reads that, so the translation keeps the source and leaves the tension with 1 Sam 17 (ESV, NASB, NRSV, NJPS, CSB do the same). Other possible meanings: (1) '[the brother of] Goliath', supplied from 1 Chr 20:5 — KJV, NIV, NET; many think Chronicles reflects the better text; (2) Elhanan as another name for David — Targum and some rabbinic and later commentators; (3) a second Philistine named Goliath, or 'Goliath' as a title — some conservative commentators.
harapha (with article) may be an eponymous ancestor or a term for the Rephaim giant clan; the KJV takes it as one individual father of all four.
